title: The Quiet Group Chat
premise: Orsen Villalobos has built a quiet life at Marsh Hollow High around one rule: be nobody. But when a mysterious group chat called The Quiet begins messaging students with predictions that come true—accidents, breakups, a teacher's resignation—Orsen realizes their own anonymous code account, 'mothlight,' may have seeded it. As the chat's predictions grow darker and the school splits into believers, deniers, and hunters, Orsen falls for Priya Raghunathan, the one person determined to unmask whoever is behind it all. In the end, Orsen must choose between staying hidden forever or claiming their creation, shutting The Quiet down before it predicts something unforgivable—accepting exposure, love, and consequence over the safe invisibility that was slowly erasing them anyway.
about_author: Oscar Thackeray is the pen name of a former software tester from the Pacific Northwest who spent a decade writing documentation nobody read before turning to fiction people might. They write stories about quiet kids, hidden systems, and the moment silence stops being safe.

chapters.title: Head Down, Grades Up
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. We meet Orsen through their meticulous invisibility system: seat choices, conversation deflection, the anonymous coding account 'mothlight' where they're actually brave. Establish the loneliness beneath the strategy. Emotional beat: the ache of being unseen even by choice.

chapters.title: The Invitation
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. An unknown number adds Orsen to a group chat called The Quiet with five other students. The first 'prediction'—that the vending machine will flood the east hallway—arrives at 9:14 p.m. Orsen dismisses it as a prank until morning. Emotional beat: wary curiosity cracking the shell of routine.

chapters.title: Water Where Water Shouldn't Be
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The hallway floods exactly as predicted; the school buzzes. Priya, student journalist, starts investigating who could have rigged it. Orsen watches from the crowd, unsettled because the prediction matched a mothlight post from months ago. Emotional beat: the first vertigo of being known.

chapters.title: Six Strangers
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Orsen maps the chat's other members: jock Dev, theater kid Wren, stoner-calm Marcus, anxious freshman Lila, and Priya, who joined to expose it. A second prediction lands—Coach Bell's resignation—and comes true within days. Emotional beat: the group feels dangerously like belonging.

chapters.title: Mothlight's Shadow
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV, with flashbacks. Orsen digs into their own archived code and finds a predictive model they abandoned—a hobby experiment that shouldn't be running. Someone found mothlight's work and weaponized it. Emotional beat: guilt curdling into fear; the past has hands.

chapters.title: The Believer's High
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. The chat starts granting small 'favors'—leaked test answers, a rival's secret. Dev becomes The Quiet's evangelist, and the school splits into factions. Orsen sees their creation becoming a currency of power. Emotional beat: seduction of influence, and its rot.

chapters.title: Priya Asks the Wrong Question
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya interviews Orsen for the school paper about the chat's 'culture of fear' and notices Orsen flinches at the right details. She doesn't accuse—she lingers. Emotional beat: first real connection, built on mutual suspicion neither will name.

chapters.title: Labels
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. The chat begins assigning members roles—Oracle, Herald, Ghost, Cleaner. Orsen is labeled Ghost: the one who watches. Lila, labeled Cleaner, is ordered to 'handle' a rumor about Wren and refuses. Emotional beat: the horror of being categorized by something you built.

chapters.title: Rooftop, No Signal
chapters.summary: Dual POV, alternating. Orsen and Priya, both sneaking off to think, collide on the roof where the wifi dies. Without screens, they talk honestly—about pressure, parents, pretending. Emotional beat: love beginning where performance ends.

chapters.title: The Prediction About Wren
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The chat predicts Wren will 'quit theater by Friday.' Pressure mounts—vandalized props, an anonymous email to the director. Wren holds on, and the group watches a prediction try to make itself true. Emotional beat: self-fulfilling prophecy as violence.

chapters.title: Ghost Protocol
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Orsen traces The Quiet's server through old mothlight infrastructure and finds a co-author's handle: someone who once emailed mothlight admiringly. The trail points toward Marsh Hollow itself. Emotional beat: hunter and hunted collapsing into one person.

chapters.title: Duty Calls, Twice
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya's editor demands she name a suspect; her family expects a journalism scholarship built on this story. Publishing would mean betraying Orsen, whom she now half-suspects and fully likes. Emotional beat: love against duty, the theme made personal.

chapters.title: Lila Breaks
chapters.summary: Lila's POV. Ordered to spread a cruel rumor to fulfill a prediction, Lila instead confesses everything to the principal—who confiscates her phone and dismisses her as hysterical. The chat punishes her with exposure of her anxiety medication. Emotional beat: the system's cruelty made flesh; the adult world fails her.

chapters.title: What the Chat Knows About Orsen
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. The Quiet messages Orsen directly: 'I know what you built, Ghost. Help me finish it, or Friday's prediction is about you.' It includes a detail only someone inside Orsen's old life could know—the co-author is revealed as Theo, Orsen's estranged former best friend and coding partner. Emotional beat: betrayal wearing a familiar face.

chapters.title: The Theo Years
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV, flashback-heavy. We learn why Orsen went invisible: a middle-school coding partnership with Theo ended when their shared project was used to humiliate a classmate, and Orsen let Theo take the blame alone. Emotional beat: the origin wound—power corrupted once, and Orsen's silence made it possible.

chapters.title: Confession on the Roof
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Orsen tells Priya everything: mothlight, the model, Theo, the guilt. Priya's response isn't forgiveness or fury—it's a plan. They'll use Orsen's backdoor into The Quiet's system to end it before Friday's prediction. Emotional beat: love as alliance, not absolution.

chapters.title: Turning the Ghost
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Orsen re-enters the chat as Ghost, feeding Theo false data while Priya rallies Dev, Wren, and Marcus to warn the targets of Friday's prediction. The group that was a weapon becomes a team. Emotional beat: belonging finally earned through risk.

chapters.title: Friday
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs, interlocking. Friday's prediction lands: 'The auditorium will burn during fourth period.' It's not arson Theo planned but a cascade—a rigged alarm test, a locked exit, panic. The five students race to undo each domino as the school watches the prediction fail in real time. Emotional beat: climax—collective action beating prophecy.

chapters.title: Unmasked
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Theo, exposed, confronts Orsen in the empty auditorium: 'You made me. You hid, and I kept building.' Orsen chooses accountability—admitting their role publicly, to Priya, to the school. Theo is expelled; the chat dies. Emotional beat: the cost of stepping out of hiding, paid willingly.

chapters.title: The Article
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya writes the full story, naming Orsen as mothlight's creator and herself as the friend who helped end it, sacrificing the 'exclusive exposé' framing her scholarship needed. Her editor kills it; she publishes independently. Emotional beat: duty redefined by love and integrity.

chapters.title: Locker Open
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Aftermath: suspension served, rumors survived, and Orsen's locker—the symbol of their sealed-off life—sticks open all week. Dev, Wren, Marcus, and Lila save them a seat. Orsen codes again, but in the open, under their own name. Emotional beat: quiet joy of being visible and chosen.

chapters.title: The Last Message
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV, epilogue. Months later, a final message arrives from an unknown number: 'The model's still out there. Someone else will find it.' Orsen looks at Priya, at the group chat now renamed and full of jokes, and replies: 'Then they'll find us ready.' Emotional beat: vigilant hope—power never sleeps, but neither do the people who learned to share it.
